what_it_does: Voltage-controlled oscillators (VCOs) are circuits that produce radio signals for wireless and high-speed wired communication. The quality of a radio signal is measured by phase noise—unwanted jitter that degrades signal clarity. This paper demonstrates a novel VCO design using pure CMOS transistors (the industry standard) that achieves exceptionally low phase noise. The innovation is a pole-convergence technique applied to a series-resonance topology, which creates very stable oscillations without the area and mismatch penalties of older multi-core approaches. The result achieves a phase-noise figure of merit (FoMTA) of 202.1 dBc/Hz, meaning the design delivers excellent signal purity at 10 MHz offset from the carrier frequency—useful for high-frequency RF and high-speed ADC/DAC applications.
